newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB, Swiss Bank tie-up to focus on Japan ventures.
newsitem.headline: LTCB, Swiss Bank tie-up to focus on Japan ventures.

text.p: Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Swiss Bank Corp said on Tuesday that a strategic alliance they announced earlier in the day will focus on Japan-based joint ventures in investment banking, asset management and private banking.

LTCB also said in a statement it was mulling, subject to board approval, raising about 200 billion yen in capital, or $1.8 billion. Of this, 130 billion yen would be raised through preferred stock and 70 billion yen would be raised through subordinated debt.
SBC Warburg will help LTCB raise the funds, while SBC will hold about 50 percent of the new LTCB preferred stock in its investment portfolio, the statement said.
In investment banking, LTCB and SBC will form a jointly managed partnership, called LTCB SBC Warburg Securities, with capital of 60 billion yen.
The partnership, to begin operation in early 1998, will be responsible for the Japanese investment banking business of both firms, combining LTCB Securities and SBC Warburg's operations in Japan.
LTCB and SBC will also set up an asset management firm, to be called LTCB SBC Brinson, and a private banking firm, to be Japan's first-ever private bank.
